survey: Saloon batwing doors in a freestanding wooden frame, seen from slightly left of front. Two square posts stand on wider base blocks that sit flat on the plank floor and cast shadows. A thick lintel plank rests on top of both posts and overhangs them a little at each end. Two half-height swinging doors hang between the posts. The left door hangs from the left post on two brass hinges, top and bottom, and is swung a little toward the camera. Its free edge looks taller and lower because it is closer, which matches the perspective. The right door hangs from the right post on two matching hinges and is nearly closed. The two doors mirror each other: an outer frame, a row of vertical slats on top, a rail, and a solid lower panel. There is a small gap where the doors meet in the middle. The doors look slightly offset in height and width, but the camera angle and the left door's swing explain this; the right post stands closer to the camera, so its parts sit lower in the frame. Every hinge plate joins a post to a door, nothing floats, and the doors could swing both ways as real batwing doors do.
